title: What their growth does to the UK

predict.q: Emerging economies grow fast. Demand for UK exports rises, and the prices of the manufactured goods the UK imports fall. What happens to UK real output and the price level?

options.s: Real output rises; the price level is certain to rise
options.fb: Cheaper imports shift SRAS right, which pulls the price level down. Try a bigger SRAS shift.

options.s: Real output rises; the price level could rise or fall
options.fb: AD right and SRAS right both raise output; they push the price level in opposite directions, so the bigger shift wins.

options.s: Real output falls; the price level is certain to fall
options.fb: Some firms lose sales, but higher export demand and lower costs raise total output in this model, and the price level falls only if the supply shift is the bigger one.

options.s: Real output stays the same; the price level falls
options.fb: More export demand shifts AD right, which raises real output.

task: Set export demand 2 and cheaper imports 1; then 1 and 2. Then add "higher commodity prices" (SRAS left).

target.do: Move the export demand and cheaper imports sliders (try 2 and 1, then 1 and 2), then press Check.

takeaway: Emerging-economy growth brings both demand and supply shocks to the UK; the net effect depends on their sizes.
